facts.claim: The Alchemist is a novel. Santiago, a young shepherd from Andalusia, travels toward the Egyptian pyramids after a recurring dream of treasure. The king Melchizedek tells him to follow omens and gives him two stones, Urim and Thummim, but tells him to rely on his own decisions.
Tribal wars in the desert stop Santiago's caravan at the oasis of Al-Fayoum, which is neutral ground: weapons are banned there.
In the desert near the oasis Santiago watches hawks flying high; one hawk attacks another. He then sees an image of an army with drawn swords riding into the oasis.
facts.source: LitCharts ('a hawk attack another'); CliffsNotes summary via search; makeheadway

facts.claim: He tells the camel driver, who tells him to go to the tribal chieftains. He warns them.
The chieftains decide the men of the oasis will break the agreement and carry arms the next day. If the warning proves false, Santiago will pay with his life; if true, he will be rewarded.

Leaving the chieftains that night, Santiago is confronted by a stranger on horseback who threatens him; Santiago says he is not afraid to die, and the stranger turns out to be the alchemist, who calls it a test of courage.
The next day about five hundred tribesmen ride into the oasis with weapons hidden under their robes; the armed men of the oasis defeat them.
Santiago receives fifty pieces of gold and is asked to become counselor of the oasis.
facts.source: LitCharts (fifty pieces of gold); CliffsNotes via search (counselor)

facts.claim: Santiago reads the vision without reasoning it out; the oasis survives and his prediction is borne out. The alchemist then takes him on as his student.
The novel ends with Santiago finding that the treasure was buried under a sycamore in the ruined church in Spain where his journey began.

Melchizedek gives Santiago two stones, Urim and Thummim, but tells him to rely on his own decisions. Earlier, in a crystal shop in Tangier, Santiago shows he has learned to read omens: seeing a tired man climbing the hill, he suggests selling tea.

rejected.claim: Santiago stood in the desert with money gone and direction lost, saw two hawks dance, fled and was saved (old text)
rejected.reason: Contradicts the novel: he did not flee; he warned the chieftains and risked his life.

rejected.claim: Quote 'The universe speaks, but only those who listen hear'
rejected.reason: Not a verified line from the novel.

rejected.claim: Coelho interprets omens as selective attention (job ads, lovers)
rejected.reason: Not in the novel; a modern psychological gloss.
